market_holds: Spot $12.73 at the 2026-11-24 close (the sealed intraday spot was $12.555), 0.5% above the 52-week low and 44% below the high. It is down 24.6% over 20 sessions, almost all of it on one day: 2026-11-12, when it gapped to $13.95 from $16.72 and closed at $12.49 (-25.3%) on 19.9M shares, about 3x the 20-day average. Hong Kong (2076.HK) followed the next session, 64.45 to 48.54 HKD (-24.7%). Since then the stock has held $12.5-13.3 on falling volume. No filing or named report explains the drop. Secondary sites cite unconfirmed talk of softer guidance, China tech weakness (Golden Dragon index -3%) and fear that AI hurts hiring. On 2026-11-13 hedge-fund skepticism was reported: the Q3 guide does not reflect the tier-1/2 price rise JPMorgan described, and paying-enterprise growth is slowing. Options (Dec-18 expiry, 24 days) price a 9.96% straddle at 53.5% ATM IV, against 95% realised 20-day vol inflated by the crash. The baseline's event-implied figure is 0 by construction, so it is not usable. My rough read is a 6-9% event move, and the past four reactions were -5.9%, -0.3% (after opening -6%), +5.5% and -6.7%. Bar: Q3 guide RMB 2.41-2.50bn (+11.4% to +15.6%), given 2026-08-25. Revenue consensus is $361.5M (Earnings Whispers, August) to $365.9M (Benzinga, mid-November), about RMB 2.44-2.47bn at today's USD/CNY of 6.66, so roughly the midpoint of the guide. EPS consensus is about $0.31. The sweep's -$0.02 row is broken. The line it trades on is the Q4 revenue guide. In November 2025 the stock fell about 6.7% on a weak Q4 guide despite a Q3 beat, and in March 2026 it fell 5.9% when growth guidance decelerated. Sell-side: Barclays cut its target from $20 to $17 and 86Research upgraded to Buy at $17, both in mid-November. Consensus target is $18 (MarketBeat). Supply overhang since September: Tencent sold about HK$2.2bn of stock (announced 2026-09-15) and the CEO sold $110M on 2026-09-21 for an offshore tax bill.
view: This is a China recruitment platform that crashed 25% two weeks before its print with no disclosed cause. It now trades at roughly 9x trailing earnings with heavy buybacks and dividends, and it reports into a quarter where the revenue bar sits at the guide midpoint. The print will resolve two things the price is torn on: whether the tier-1/2 price rise from Q3 shows up in revenue (a Q3 landing at or above the RMB 2.50bn top), and what the Q4 guide says. Q4 2025 was about RMB 2.085bn by my arithmetic, and sell-side full-year models of about RMB 9.27bn imply roughly RMB 2.34bn, or +12%. The company's record on its own guide is mixed. It beat the top for Q4 2025 (2.085 vs 2.05-2.07) but landed mid-range for Q2 2026 (2.399 vs 2.38-2.42). The macro read for Q4 is mildly better: China youth unemployment fell from 18.9% in August to 17.2% in October, and urban unemployment was 5.1% in October. After a -25% gap on no news, inline numbers with a ~12% Q4 guide would likely bring a relief bounce, so the asymmetry leans slightly up. Against that, a gap that large with Hong Kong following suggests someone sold on information. The date was set late (2026-11-25 against 2025-11-18 last year) and only announced the day after the crash. October brought a system outage and a run of complaints. The Q4 guide has been the line that sank the last two weak reactions. I cannot show what the crash priced, so I cannot show that the rumoured soft guide is fully in the price. Net: a slight lean up, nowhere near a bet.

recommendation.reason: The print turns on the Q4 revenue guide and on whether the tier-1/2 price rise lifts Q3 above the guide midpoint. I found no dated, independent data since the August call that shows either beyond what the 2026-11-12 crash and the consensus already hold. The relief-rally setup after an unexplained 25% drop is real but symmetric to the risk that the drop was informed, so the 65% bar is not met.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide of about RMB 2.35bn or more (+13% or better) with Q3 at or above RMB 2.50bn would make a long the right call. A Q4 guide at or below about +9%, or a falling paying-enterprise count, would confirm the rumour and favour the short side.

self_critique: The strongest case for the short side: a 25% gap with nothing disclosed, Hong Kong following, a report date a week later than last year and announced only after the crash, a slowing paying-enterprise count, and two of the last four prints sold off on guidance. That pattern often means informed selling ahead of a real disappointment. The strongest case for the long side: the stock already trades about 9x with a large cash pile and buybacks, the rumour is in the price, and mid-range numbers would squeeze it. Both cases are plausible and neither can be shown, which is why I stay at 55 with no action.
